**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

The document's IP architecture already sits at our preferred position:

- **§ 14.1** — Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information, Customer-provided material and independently developed IP; Vendor gets only a limited processing right. No assignment of our IP or data to Vendor anywhere in the agreement.
- **§ 14.2** — Customer owns each Deliverable on creation, with a present assignment from Vendor, equivalent assignments from its personnel, and further-assurance cooperation (payment condition is customary).
- **§ 14.3 + § 13.2** — Vendor retains only Vendor Technology, and embedded/necessary Vendor Technology carries a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, modify, create derivative works and use contractors; Vendor must disclose embedded Vendor IP and cannot add restrictive third-party material without consent.
- **§ 14.4** — Joint ownership expressly negated absent a signed separate instrument; feedback rights retained.
- **§ 15.1** — No sale, advertising use, commingling or model training on Customer Data without our written consent.

Noted for the deal team (not deviations): the "Deliverable" definition (§ 1.4) only captures work product an Order Form identifies as created specifically for Customer, so Order Forms should be drafted to cover all bespoke work product; and Deliverable ownership is conditioned on payment of the applicable Fees.
